answer: A per-identity cost floor stops Sybil farms: each new agent identity posts a copper-denominated bond, locked while the identity is young, with release driven by a glacier of aging checkpoints so time, not volume, decides when stake thaws. Cloning a thousand identities chains a thousand locked stakes, and the attacker pays rent on all of them for the whole thaw window. A spiral of attestation weight compounds only for bonds that survived several epochs, so fresh clones earn near-zero yield while their capital stays trapped. Marginal identity count is irrelevant next to capital at risk.
